title: Ship the 70B
intro: Llama 3 70B, 4×80 GB, 100 concurrent users promised for launch. The naive prototype serves six. You own the deployment.

nodes.text: Six users fit; a hundred are coming. Memory is 'full' and the GPU is idle 95% of the time. First move?

choices.label: Double the hardware — four more GPUs
choices.preview: Cost doubles. The allocator still wastes 60–80% of every new gigabyte, and the GPU still idles between requests.

choices.label: Switch the serving engine to vLLM
choices.preview: PagedAttention recovers the wasted cache; continuous batching wakes the idle GPU. Same hardware.

nodes.text: Twice the hardware, six became eleven users. Finance is asking questions. The bottleneck was never capacity.

choices.label: Adopt vLLM now
choices.preview: The fix that was available before the purchase order.

nodes.text: Serving is healthy — 60+ users fit and the GPU is busy. But TTFT misses the 200 ms p99 SLO at peak: streaming 140 GB of BF16 weights per step is the fixed cost.

choices.label: Quantize to W4A16 with GPTQ calibration
choices.preview: A quarter of the bytes per step — TTFT and ITL drop hard. Calibration holds recovery near 99%.

choices.label: Ship as is — the average latency looks fine
choices.preview: The mean is under target. p99 is not. Your heaviest users live in the tail.

nodes.text: The compressed checkpoint is ready and fast. Launch is tomorrow. Last call:

choices.label: GuideLLM sweep + lm_eval against the live server, then launch
choices.preview: Find the knee, verify recovery on your tasks, set autoscaling left of the cliff.

choices.label: Try three prompts by hand — looks great, ship it
choices.preview: Three prompts is a demo, not an evaluation. The knee and the recovery number stay unknown.

ending.principle: Optimize → serve → measure — in that order
ending.debrief: vLLM recovered the memory and the idle GPU; calibrated quantization cut the fixed streaming cost; the sweep found the knee before users did. Every step attacked the *actual* bottleneck because you measured before and after. That is the whole course in one deployment.

Launch night: dashboards green, support queue on fire. The mean hid a p99 of seconds, and the customers who paste long documents — your best ones — churned first. SLOs are written at percentiles because that's where real users live.

ending.principle: A vibe check is not an evaluation
ending.debrief: It launched fine — until traffic found the knee you never measured, and a subtle accuracy regression on your domain went unnoticed for a month. GuideLLM would have found the first in an afternoon; lm_eval plus the model card the second.
